lead.headline: Bitcoin slips under $65,000 as Asian chip stocks slide
lead.standfirst: Bitcoin gave back its weekend bounce overnight as chipmakers in Taiwan and South Korea fell ahead of Nvidia's results, in a week packed with Fed and AI tests.
body: Bitcoin traded near $64,500 on Kraken at 06:30 UK on Monday, down from about $65,315 at the weekly close at midnight. The overnight low was near $64,240. Zcash fell from about $915 to near $884, touching $872.

The weakness came as Asian technology shares sold off. Taiwan's Taiex fell 4.1% and South Korea's Kospi 2.8%, while Japan's Nikkei lost 1.6%, the Associated Press reported, ahead of Nvidia's third-quarter results on Tuesday, its first since chief executive Jensen Huang resigned last week.

The Financial Times reported that Huang has discussed returning, Cointelegraph said, citing the newspaper. Nvidia's market value has fallen from about $5.8 trillion in early October to $3.9 trillion, Reuters reported.

In crypto, Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao denied on X that the exchange had sold crypto, The Block reported. He pointed to spot ETF outflows, expectations of another Fed rate hike and investors raising cash for Anthropic's share sale. More than $2 billion of positions were liquidated in the 24 hours to Sunday morning US time, according to CoinGlass data cited by The Block.

Rate pressure is the backdrop. US ten-year Treasury yields held near 5.14% after their biggest weekly fall in prices since April 2025, and futures price a quarter-point Fed hike in December as all but certain, Reuters reported. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh speaks at about 17:00 UK today.

headline: Bitcoin slipped to about $64,500 overnight as Asian chip stocks fell ahead of Nvidia's results. Rates stay the backdrop, with Fed Chair Warsh speaking this evening UK time.
spoken: Cryptonaire Post, morning edition. Bitcoin closed the week near sixty-five thousand three hundred dollars but slipped overnight to about sixty-four thousand five hundred, still above last weekend's low near sixty-two thousand. Zcash eased to about eight hundred and eighty-four dollars. Asian chip stocks fell hard ahead of Nvidia's results on Tuesday, with Taiwan down four percent. Binance's founder denied rumours the exchange had been selling. US ten-year yields hold above five percent, and markets expect a Fed rate hike in December. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh speaks at about five this evening UK time, and the day's ETF flows follow after the US close. Information only, not advice.

stories.title: Bitcoin slips back under $65,000 after the weekly close
stories.why: Bitcoin closed the week near $65,315 on Kraken, then traded between about $64,240 and $65,470 overnight and stood near $64,500 at 06:30 UK, below $64,940 at the evening edition. It remains about $2,500 above the weekend's four-month low near $62,000.

note.read: The bounce from $62,000 has stalled rather than reversed; overnight selling lined up with the drop in Asian tech shares, so bitcoin is still trading as a risk asset.
note.alt: Thin Monday-morning liquidity can exaggerate small moves, so the dip may say little until the US session opens.
note.change: A break back below $62,000, or a return to ETF inflows on Monday, would change the picture.

stories.title: Asian chip stocks slide ahead of Nvidia's results
stories.why: Taiwan's Taiex fell 4.1%, the Kospi 2.8% and the Nikkei 1.6% on Monday, the Associated Press reported. Nvidia reports on Tuesday after the US close, its first results since Jensen Huang's resignation; options imply a move of about 7% either way, Reuters reported. Bitcoin has moved with tech shares through this sell-off.
stories.caveat: Reuters' earlier Sydney report had smaller falls and slightly higher US futures; the AP figures are later in the session.

note.read: Nvidia's results on Tuesday are now the main risk-appetite test of the week, ahead of the Fed minutes and Anthropic's listing.
note.alt: The selling may be specific to Nvidia's leadership crisis and chip-export questions rather than broad risk aversion.
note.change: A calm Nvidia report and a stable Nasdaq would ease the pressure on crypto from this side.

stories.title: Yields hold above 5% with a December Fed hike priced in
stories.why: The US ten-year yield was flat near 5.14% and the two-year near 4.87% after last week's sharp rise, and the dollar index was steady near 103.4, Reuters reported. Fed funds futures treat a quarter-point hike in December as essentially locked in. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh gives opening remarks at a San Francisco Fed conference at about 17:00 UK, crypto.news reported.
stories.caveat: The speech time comes from one outlet; check the Fed's calendar.

stories.title: CZ denies Binance sold crypto during the slide
stories.why: Changpeng Zhao wrote on X that Binance did not sell crypto after its October hack and that he had bought some himself, The Block reported. He blamed ETF outflows, Fed hike expectations, cash raised for Anthropic's IPO and hack worries. CoinGlass data showed about $2.02 billion liquidated in the 24 hours to Sunday morning US time, mostly longs.
stories.caveat: CZ's statement is a claim by an interested party and cannot be checked independently.

stories.title: Zcash eases below $900 as the grants poll opens
stories.why: Zcash fell from about $915 at midnight to near $884 at 06:30 UK on Kraken, touching $872, against $899 at the evening edition. The advisory poll on the future of Zcash Community Grants was due to open today, according to the Zcash forum; no results yet.

stories.title: ETF outflow streak still awaits Monday's data
stories.why: No new flow data overnight. US spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $1.91 billion over seven straight sessions to 13 November, according to Farside Investors figures cited by crypto.news. Monday's flows land after the US close.

explained.title: What "implied move" means for Nvidia
body: Options traders price how far a share is likely to move after an event. When Reuters says Nvidia's options imply a move of about 7% either way, it means the cost of options that profit from a big move, in either direction, adds up to roughly that size of swing. It is a price for uncertainty, not a forecast of direction.
It matters for bitcoin because big moves in Nvidia have lately coincided with moves in risk assets generally, so a larger-than-implied move could spill over.

investigating: Was $62,000 the low of this leg? Evidence: whether bitcoin holds above $62,000 through Monday and Tuesday's US sessions.
Will ETF outflows run to an eighth day? Evidence: Farside and SoSoValue figures for Monday 16 November.
